claims.text: The McGurk effect is a phenomenon where the perception of speech is influenced by visual input, such as a video of a person mouthing different phonemes than what is heard.
An example of the McGurk effect is when the audio of the phoneme 'baa' is paired with a video of someone mouthing 'vaa', leading viewers to perceive 'vaa' or 'gaa'.
The susceptibility to the McGurk effect varies, with a higher illusionability observed at the word level compared to the sentence level due to contextual influences.
